newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Consensus on Iraqi flight eludes U.N. committee.
newsitem.headline: Consensus on Iraqi flight eludes U.N. committee.

text.p: The Security Council's Iraqi sanctions committee failed to reach consensus on Thursday on whether Iraq violated sanctions by sending a plane with pilgrims to Saudi Arabia, committee sources said.
This made it unlikely that the council itself, relying on the committee's findings, would be able to issue an agreed statement criticising the Iraqi action, as called for by the United States.
The sanctions committee has the same 15-nation makeup as the Security Council and its chairman is the council's president this month, ambassador Antonio Monteiro of Portugal.
At issue is a flight from Baghdad to Jeddah and back on Wednesday that took 104 pilgrims to Saudi Arabia for the annual haj to Mecca.

American U.N. envoy Bill Richardson told reporters on Wednesday the flight was "an outright violation of sanctions" imposed on Iraq shortly after its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait and that the United States was seeking a "very strong (council) presidential statement."
The council cannot issue statements unless they are agreed by all 15 members, giving each in effect a veto.

One source said that, while there were differences of opinion in the sanctions committee over whether one or both legs of the Iraqi flight between Baghdad and Jeddah violated sanctions, China took the view that neither was a violation.
